messages:
Aditi: CI red on PR #456 — only failing on matrix shard 'integration:py38-matrix-3'. Can someone rerun just that job? I don't want a full rebuild since the image should be cached.

Aditi: log snippet:
```
E   requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: Read timed out.
...tests/integration/test_auth.py::test_user_auth_flow
```

Ben: You can do a targeted retry without rebuilding using our ci-cli: 
```
ci retry --pr 456 --job integration:py38-matrix-3 --no-image-build
```
That will reuse the existing image and restart the job. If you don't have ci-cli installed, you can use GH actions as a fallback:
```
# list recent runs for the PR
gh run list --branch=pr/456 --workflow=integration-matrix.yml
# rerun a specific run (replace <run-id>)
gh run rerun <run-id> --job integration:py38-matrix-3
```

Jules: FYI gh run rerun may spin up a fresh runner and might not preserve the host volume cache. If you need to guarantee the same worker (and preserve build artifacts), restart on the same worker with Buildkite: 
```
bk restart --job=integration:py38-matrix-3 --preserve-volume
```
(Caveat: --preserve-volume is only supported on ephemeral workers that are still alive.)

CI-bot: Buildkite job 987654 restarted by Ben.

Aditi: Ran the ci retry command, it started and looks like the job is queued. Thanks :raised_hands:

Ben: If it flakes again, we can bisect the regression with: 
```
ci bisect --test test_user_auth_flow --range HEAD~30..HEAD
```
Will run the test across commits to isolate the breaking change.

Aditi: Good call. Also — where's the short list of ci-cli flags?

Ben: docs/ci/quick-retry.md has the flags. TL;DR: --no-image-build, --preserve-volume, --keep-kv-cache. Don't use --preserve-volume on production database migrations.

Aditi: Got it. I'll wait for the retry result and mark this thread resolved when green.
